name: P2P baseline
description: Generic purchase-to-pay norm derived from the failure-mode catalogue of the p2p pack. Activity parameters are canonical ids (p2p.*) to be translated through the activity mapping; thresholds are placeholders flagged uncalibrated in metadata.meta and must be set by the owners on the empirical distributions.

notes: Lag constraints use missing_b='censor' so that open items are scored by their age instead of as full violations.
Applicability uses the variant ids of stages.yaml as flow_type values; derive flow_type with a recipe before scoring.
The requisition-presence constraint applies only where the organisation requires requisitions; restrict its applicability to those document types.
sources: Jessen, Fahland, Zerbato, WISE, BPIC 2019 norm

guidance.source: guidance.yaml of the pack (generic tier); the project overlay is stored with the project

closure.expectation: Every ordered item is received, invoiced and paid, so that nothing stays open longer than it should.
closure.meaning_when_missed: An item is missing one of its expected milestones: goods were ordered but no receipt is posted, goods were received but no invoice arrived, or an invoice was recorded but never cleared.
closure.why_it_matters: Open items hide liabilities and unpaid vendors, distort accruals at period end and make the purchase order history unusable for planning; every open item is a call, an e-mail or a manual clean-up later.
closure.how_detected: Three presence rules on the flows where the milestone is expected: invoice evidence on invoice-bearing items, a payment on invoice-bearing items, and a goods or service receipt on three-way items. Items still open at the end of the data are flagged separately as not yet judgeable.

usual_reasons.check: share of items whose last event is within 60 days of the window end, per group; read the shortfall only after excluding them

usual_reasons.check: goods received without invoice evidence after 60 days, by vendor; invoice documents without item link in the source system

usual_reasons.check: service items with an invoice but no service entry sheet, by purchasing group

usual_reasons.text: The item was deleted, blocked or closed by reducing the quantity instead of receiving it
usual_reasons.check: deletion, block and quantity-change events on the open items

usual_reasons.text: The item category expects a milestone that this purchase never has (framework, consignment)
usual_reasons.check: ask the buyer whether the document type needs a receipt or an item-level clearing at all

usual_actions.text: Period-end review of open items with the buyers, closing or correcting each with a reason
Dunning of missing invoices for received goods and a mandatory order reference on incoming invoices

Exclude censored items from the reading and set the observation window in the run

flow_discipline.missed_label: steps out of order for this flow type
flow_discipline.missed_label_de: Schritte in falscher Reihenfolge für diesen Flusstyp
flow_discipline.expectation: Requisition, order, receipt and invoice happen in the order the flow type prescribes: in GR-based flows the invoice follows the receipt, in invoice-first flows the payment block is released only after the goods arrive, two-way and consignment items show no postings they should not have.
flow_discipline.meaning_when_missed: Goods or services were bought or paid outside the agreed channel, an invoice was processed before delivery was confirmed, a block was released before the goods arrived, or an item is typed as a flow it does not follow.
flow_discipline.why_it_matters: Off-contract prices, no leverage over the vendor, payment for goods not received, audit findings on the three-way match, and repair work in accounts payable to fix documents after the fact.
flow_discipline.how_detected: Order rules per flow type: invoice evidence not before the first receipt in GR-based flows; payment block released after the first receipt in invoice-first flows; no receipt postings on two-way items; no item-level clearing on consignment items.

usual_reasons.text: Urgent needs bypass the requisition and the buyer
usual_reasons.check: ask the requesters and the category manager which spend areas run on phone orders

approval.missed_label: ordered without or long before approval
approval.missed_label_de: ohne oder lange vor Genehmigung bestellt
approval.expectation: Every order that needs a requisition has one, and requisitions and orders are released within the agreed days without repeated re-approval.
approval.meaning_when_missed: An order went out without the required request and release, the release took longer than agreed, or the order was changed so often that it needed approval again and again.
approval.why_it_matters: Spending outside the budget owner's sight, delayed deliveries while the release queue waits, and approvers re-reading the same order after every change.
approval.how_detected: Presence of a requisition or shopping cart where the document type requires one; days from requisition and order creation to their release against a target; count of approval changes per item.

timeliness.missed_label_de: zu lange Wartezeit zwischen den Schritten
timeliness.expectation: Receipts, invoices, block releases and payments follow each other within the agreed number of days.
timeliness.meaning_when_missed: Items age between two steps; invoices wait for a receipt or a release, released invoices wait for a payment run, and vendors wait for their money.
timeliness.why_it_matters: Lost early-payment discounts, vendor escalations and delivery stops, working capital tied up or paid out too early, and a backlog that accounts payable works through by hand.
timeliness.how_detected: Time-between-steps rules with a target and a tolerance: receipt to invoice in GR-based flows (target 10 days, tolerance to 30 in the paper's norm), invoice to payment (30 days, tolerance to 90), receipt to block release and release to payment in invoice-first flows (2 and 5 days). Each item scores between met and fully missed according to how far beyond the target it is.

usual_reasons.text: Payment runs on fixed dates and cash-management holds at period end
usual_reasons.check: ask accounts payable for the payment-run calendar and any period-end holds

rework.expectation: Each step is posted once and stays; no repeated receipts, invoices, approvals, confirmations or term changes on the same item.
rework.meaning_when_missed: The same step was posted several times or changed afterwards, so the item was handled more than once and its history is unstable.
rework.why_it_matters: Every repeat is a manual touch, a matching problem and a chance for a duplicate payment; unstable commitments make planning and vendor evaluation unreliable.
rework.how_detected: Count rules with a tolerated number and a saturation point: receipt events (more than two count), invoice receipts (more than one), approval changes (any), payment-term changes (any), vendor confirmations and confirmed-date changes in the baseline.

usual_reasons.check: change events preceding each repeat

exceptions.expectation: Cancellations of receipts and invoices, item deletions, blocks and vendor memos are the exception, not part of the normal path.
exceptions.meaning_when_missed: A posting had to be undone or corrected with a separate document; the item did not go straight through.
exceptions.why_it_matters: Corrections cost effort in the warehouse and in accounts payable, they delay payment, they carry audit risk, and memos signal disputes with the vendor.
exceptions.how_detected: Rules that expect an activity never to occur: cancelled invoice receipt, cancelled goods receipt, deleted item, vendor debit memo, vendor credit memo, and in the baseline item blocks, manual payment blocks and interface failures.

value.missed_label: price or quantity changed after ordering
value.missed_label_de: Preis oder Menge nach Bestellung geändert
value.expectation: The price and quantity on the order are the ones agreed with the vendor before ordering, and invoiced values match ordered and received values, especially on high-value items.
value.meaning_when_missed: The order was edited after it went out, or correction documents moved the value of the item; what is paid may not be what was agreed.
value.why_it_matters: Money paid above the agreed price, no audit trail of the negotiation, and invoice verification that passes because the order was changed to fit the invoice.
value.how_detected: Count rules on price and quantity changes (any change counts, two saturate), value-weighted rules that count memos and price changes more on high-exposure items, and the spread of the cumulative net worth across the item's postings; these are commercial-risk indicators, not audit findings.

effort.expectation: Items pass from order to payment with as few manual touches, hand-offs and events as the flow needs.
effort.meaning_when_missed: People had to intervene several times on the item, several people touched it, or the item collected a long chain of events.
effort.why_it_matters: Effort in purchasing and accounts payable, waiting time at each hand-off, and errors introduced by manual work; the touchless rate is the lever for automation.
effort.how_detected: Threshold rules on derived counts: manual touches by named users (more than 4, saturating at 10), distinct human users (more than 2), total events (more than 10) and the manual share of events (above half); batch users are excluded by name.

usual_reasons.check: user names of the most frequent touches; batch or system users in the resource column

b_closure_invoice_present.expectation: Every purchase order item that is meant to be invoiced shows invoice evidence, either an invoice posted in the system or an invoice dated by the vendor.
b_closure_invoice_present.meaning_when_missed: Goods or services were ordered (and often received) but no invoice is on record for the item.
b_closure_invoice_present.why_it_matters: Unrecorded liabilities at period end, vendors that are not paid and escalate, and a purchase order history that cannot be closed.
b_closure_invoice_present.how_detected: A presence rule on invoice-bearing flow types (three-way and two-way); consignment items are out of scope. Items open at the end of the data need the censoring caveat.

b_closure_clear_present.expectation: Every invoice-bearing item is eventually cleared by a payment.

b_flow_invoice_after_goods.expectation: In GR-based three-way flows the invoice, whether posted or dated by the vendor, does not precede the first goods or service receipt.
b_flow_invoice_after_goods.meaning_when_missed: Invoice evidence exists before any receipt on an item whose flow type says the receipt comes first.
b_flow_invoice_after_goods.why_it_matters: The three-way match cannot be completed at posting, invoices are blocked or paid on trust, and the flow type is not what the vendor actually does.
b_flow_invoice_after_goods.how_detected: An order rule on GR-based items comparing the first invoice evidence (posting or vendor invoice date, merged) with the first receipt. Norm draft v1.1 therefore splits it into a commercial and a compliance expectation.

constraints.description: Invoice evidence should exist for invoice-bearing flows.
Invoice-bearing flows should eventually be cleared.
Three-way and service flows should contain receipt evidence.
In GR-based flows invoice evidence should not precede the first receipt.
In invoice-first flows the payment block release should follow the receipt.
Two-way items should not show receipt postings.
Consignment items are settled periodically, not cleared per item.
Requisition or shopping-cart evidence should precede the order (restrict applicability to document types that require one).
Requisitions should be released within a target time (uncalibrated).
Orders should be released within a target time (uncalibrated).
Re-approvals after changes should be rare.
In GR-based flows the invoice should follow the receipt within a target time.
Invoices should clear within terms; open invoices are scored by their age.
Goods should arrive within the planned lead time; open items are scored by their age (replace delta by days beyond the scheduled date where available).
Released invoices should clear quickly.
Too many receipt events indicate fragmentation.
Repeated invoice receipts indicate invoice handling churn.
Vendor confirmations beyond the tolerated number indicate unstable commitments.
Delivery-date changes after ordering should be rare.
Payment-term changes on the order should be rare.
Invoice cancellations should be exceptional.
Goods receipt cancellations should be exceptional.
Item deletion should be exceptional once execution is underway.
Item blocks should be exceptional.
Manual payment blocks should be exceptional outside invoice-first flows.
Vendor memos should be rare.
Interface transfer failures should not occur.
Price changes after item creation indicate commercial inconsistency risk.
Quantity changes after the first receipt indicate commercial inconsistency risk.
Invoices should not precede the order item.
Too many manual touches reduce touchless processing potential.
Very long event chains indicate execution friction.
